rounds.t: Pancreas and spleen embryology, retroperitoneal structures

q.s: A 2-day-old with Down syndrome has bilious vomiting. Imaging shows a ring of pancreatic tissue encircling the second part of the duodenum. Abnormal migration of which structure causes this?
e: Correct. Abnormal rotation of the ventral bud forms an annular pancreas around the 2nd part of the duodenum.
Wrong. The ventral bud is responsible.
Wrong. Forms the liver and biliary tree.

q.s: Which part of the pancreas is derived solely from the ventral pancreatic bud?
e: Correct. The ventral bud forms the uncinate process; both buds contribute to the head and main duct.

q.s: A 35-year-old woman has recurrent pancreatitis without gallstones or alcohol use. MRCP shows the dorsal pancreatic duct draining most of the gland through the minor papilla. What is the embryologic cause?
o: Ectopic pancreatic tissue in the stomach
Failure of the ventral and dorsal ducts to fuse (pancreas divisum)
e: Correct. Separate drainage through a small minor papilla may cause pancreatitis.

q.s: In pancreas divisum, the dorsal duct drains into which structure?
e: Correct. The dorsal (dominant) duct drains via the minor papilla; the ventral duct via the major papilla.

q.s: The spleen develops in which structure, and from which germ layer?
e: Correct. The spleen is mesodermal but supplied by a foregut artery (splenic from the celiac trunk).

q.s: Despite being mesodermal, the spleen receives blood from which source?
o: Celiac trunk via the splenic artery

q.s: A man is stabbed in the back. CT shows blood in the retroperitoneum. Which injured structure is retroperitoneal?
e: Correct. The duodenum (2nd–4th parts) is retroperitoneal (SAD PUCKER).

q.s: Which part of the pancreas is NOT retroperitoneal?
e: Correct. The tail lies in the splenorenal ligament (intraperitoneal).

q.s: Which colon segments are retroperitoneal?
A blunt trauma patient has free gas around the right kidney on CT without free intraperitoneal air. Injury to which structure is most likely?
e: Correct. Retroperitoneal duodenal rupture leaks gas into the retroperitoneum.

q.s: The mnemonic SAD PUCKER lists retroperitoneal structures. Which is included?
e: Correct. Suprarenals, Aorta/IVC, Duodenum (2–4), Pancreas (not tail), Ureters, Colon (asc/desc), Kidneys, Esophagus, Rectum (partly).

q.s: Which structure is retroperitoneal?
Annular pancreas is most strongly associated with which condition?
Both pancreatic buds contribute to which structures?
o: Pancreatic head and main pancreatic duct

q.s: The pancreas is derived from which embryologic gut region?
The ventral and dorsal pancreatic ducts normally fuse at about which week of development?
e: Correct. Failure at 7 weeks leads to pancreas divisum.

q.s: Which kidney-related structure is retroperitoneal?
o: Peritoneal surface of the bladder dome

q.s: A patient with pancreatitis has fluid tracking into the left flank (Grey Turner sign). This reflects the pancreas lying in which space?
e: Correct. Most of the pancreas is retroperitoneal, so hemorrhagic fluid tracks to the flanks.

q.s: Which part of the rectum is retroperitoneal?
o: Part of it (the rectum is partially retroperitoneal)

q.s: The esophagus in the abdomen is classified as:

During cholecystectomy, brisk bleeding occurs from the liver. The surgeon compresses the hepatoduodenal ligament in the omental foramen (Pringle maneuver). Bleeding continues. What is the most likely source?
e: Wrong. Controlled by the Pringle maneuver.
Correct. Pringle compresses inflow (portal vein, hepatic artery); persistent bleeding suggests outflow (hepatic veins, IVC).
Wrong. Controlled by the Pringle maneuver.

q.s: Which ligament contains the portal triad?
e: Correct. Proper hepatic artery, portal vein and common bile duct.

q.s: The ligamentum teres hepatis, a remnant of the fetal umbilical vein, lies in which ligament?
e: Correct. Connects liver to the anterior abdominal wall.

q.s: The short gastric arteries run in which ligament?
e: Correct. Short gastrics and left gastroepiploic vessels.

q.s: The tail of the pancreas is found in which ligament?
e: Correct. Along with the splenic artery and vein.

q.s: A surgeon divides a ligament between the liver and the lesser curvature of the stomach to enter the lesser sac. Which ligament?
e: Correct. Part of the lesser omentum; may be cut to access the lesser sac.

q.s: The omental (epiploic) foramen connecting the greater and lesser sacs is bordered anteriorly by which ligament?
The gastroepiploic arteries run in which ligament?
e: Correct. Part of the greater omentum.

q.s: Which ligaments are derivatives of the ventral mesentery?
Which ligament separates the greater and lesser sacs on the left?
e: Wrong. Separates them on the right.

q.s: The lesser omentum consists of which ligaments?
The greater omentum includes which ligaments?
In portal hypertension, recanalized veins near the umbilicus lie within which ligament?
The splenic artery and vein travel within which ligament?
The left and right gastric arteries run in which ligament?
e: Correct. Gastric vessels along the lesser curvature.

q.s: The splenorenal ligament is derived from which embryologic structure?
During splenectomy, the surgeon divides the gastrosplenic ligament. Which vessels must be ligated?
o: Short gastric and left gastroepiploic vessels

q.s: The hepatoduodenal ligament connects which structures?
Which ligament is a derivative of the dorsal mesentery and part of the greater omentum, connecting the greater curvature to the spleen?
A clamp placed across the hepatoduodenal ligament would occlude which structures?
o: Proper hepatic artery, portal vein and common bile duct
e: Wrong. Outflow, not in the ligament.

rounds.t: Gut wall layers and digestive tract histology

q.s: A gastric lesion on biopsy involves only the mucosa and does not extend beyond the muscularis mucosae. What is it called?
e: Correct. Erosions are confined to the mucosa; ulcers extend into the submucosa or deeper.

q.s: Which nerve plexus lies in the submucosa and regulates secretion and local blood flow?
Loss of which plexus causes the motility failure in achalasia and Hirschsprung disease?
e: Correct. Located between inner circular and outer longitudinal muscle; controls motility.

q.s: List the layers of the gut wall from inside to outside.
Retroperitoneal portions of the gut have which outermost layer?
The basal electric rhythm (slow waves) of the GI tract originates in which cells, and where is it fastest?
o: Smooth muscle of the stomach; stomach

q.s: A biopsy of the esophagus normally shows which epithelium?
The upper third of the esophagus has which muscle type?
e: Correct. Middle and lower 2/3 are smooth muscle.

q.s: Which submucosal glands secrete bicarbonate-rich mucus and identify the duodenum on biopsy?
e: Wrong. Lymphoid aggregates in the ileum.

q.s: Paneth cells in the crypts of Lieberkühn secrete which substances?
A small intestine biopsy shows villi and prominent submucosal lymphoid aggregates (Peyer patches) with the largest number of goblet cells. Which segment?
e: Wrong. Tall plicae, no Peyer patches.

q.s: A biopsy shows crypts with abundant goblet cells but no villi. Which segment?
On barium study, which segment has a "feathered" appearance from numerous tall plicae circulares?
On H&E, gastric parietal cells and chief cells appear how?
o: Parietal cells eosinophilic (pink); chief cells basophilic
Parietal cells basophilic; chief cells eosinophilic

q.s: Which cells in the crypts of Lieberkühn replace enterocytes and goblet cells?
e: Wrong. Antigen sampling over Peyer patches.

q.s: The muscularis externa consists of which layers?
o: Inner circular and outer longitudinal, with the myenteric plexus between

q.s: Plicae circulares begin in which part of the small intestine?
e: Correct. Present through the proximal ileum.

q.s: The lamina propria is part of which layer?
e: Correct. Mucosa = epithelium, lamina propria, muscularis mucosae.

q.s: Villi and microvilli in the duodenum serve to:
A biopsy from the transition zone of the esophagus shows both skeletal and smooth muscle fibers. Where was the biopsy most likely taken?
o: Around the junction of the upper and middle thirds
e: Correct. Striated muscle in the upper 1/3 gives way to smooth muscle in the middle and lower 2/3, with overlap at the transition.

rounds.t: Abdominal aorta, watershed areas, and GI blood supply

q.s: An 80-year-old woman has abdominal pain and bloody diarrhea after an episode of septic shock. Colonoscopy shows ischemic mucosa at the splenic flexure. Why is this site vulnerable?
o: It is supplied only by the celiac trunk
It has no collateral flow at all
It is drained by the portal vein
It is a watershed area between SMA and IMA territories
e: Correct. Watershed regions (splenic flexure, rectosigmoid junction) are prone to ischemia in hypotension.

q.s: The rectosigmoid junction is a watershed between which vessels?
o: The last sigmoid artery (IMA) and the superior rectal artery

q.s: A 24-year-old thin man has left flank pain, gross hematuria and a left varicocele. CT shows compression of a vein between the SMA and aorta. Diagnosis?
e: Correct. The left renal vein is compressed between the SMA and aorta.

q.s: Why does nutcracker syndrome cause a left-sided varicocele?
o: The SMA compresses the testicular artery
The right gonadal vein drains into the left renal vein
The left gonadal vein drains into the compressed left renal vein
The left gonadal vein drains into the IVC
e: Correct. Back-pressure dilates the pampiniform plexus.
Wrong. That is the right side.

q.s: A 19-year-old woman who lost 15 kg rapidly with an eating disorder has postprandial epigastric pain, early satiety and bilious vomiting. Imaging shows obstruction of the third part of the duodenum. Mechanism?
o: Compression of the duodenum between the SMA and aorta after loss of mesenteric fat

q.s: Arteries supplying GI structures differ from those supplying non-GI structures in which way?
o: GI arteries are single and branch anteriorly; non-GI arteries are paired and branch laterally/posteriorly
GI arteries arise from the iliac arteries
GI arteries are paired and branch laterally

q.s: The midgut is supplied by which artery at which vertebral level?
Parasympathetic innervation of the hindgut comes from which source?
The IMA arises at which vertebral level?
Which three arteries arise from the celiac trunk?
o: Common hepatic, splenic and left gastric
Left gastric, right gastric and short gastrics
Common hepatic, SMA and left gastric

q.s: A posterior duodenal ulcer erodes into an artery and causes massive bleeding. Which artery?
e: Correct. Lies behind the first part of the duodenum.

q.s: The short gastric arteries arise from which artery?
The cystic artery usually arises from which vessel?
The right gastroepiploic artery is a branch of which artery?
Sympathetic innervation of the gut arises from which ganglia?
o: Prevertebral celiac, superior mesenteric and inferior mesenteric ganglia

q.s: The liver, gallbladder, pancreas and spleen are supplied by which artery?
e: Correct. Foregut supply (spleen is mesodermal but celiac-supplied).

q.s: The pharynx receives which innervation pattern according to the gut table?
e: Wrong. Pharynx has vagal innervation only.

q.s: Which structures receive blood from both the celiac trunk and SMA via the pancreaticoduodenal arcades?
o: Head of the pancreas and duodenum
e: Correct. Superior (celiac) and inferior (SMA) pancreaticoduodenal arteries anastomose.

q.s: Which colonic regions are watershed areas?
SMA syndrome is typically associated with which condition?
o: Rapid weight loss or low body weight
e: Correct. Loss of mesenteric fat narrows the aortomesenteric angle.

rounds.t: Portosystemic anastomoses and the pectinate line

q.s: A 56-year-old man with alcohol-associated cirrhosis vomits large amounts of bright red blood. Endoscopy shows bleeding varices in the distal esophagus. Which portosystemic anastomosis is involved?
o: Left gastric vein ↔ esophageal veins draining to the azygos
e: Correct. Esophageal varices form at this anastomosis in portal hypertension.
Wrong. That is a TIPS shunt.

q.s: A patient with portal hypertension has dilated veins radiating from the umbilicus. Which veins connect here?
o: Paraumbilical veins and small epigastric veins of the abdominal wall

q.s: Anorectal varices in portal hypertension arise at the anastomosis between which veins?
o: Superior rectal ↔ middle and inferior rectal veins
e: Correct. Superior rectal drains to the portal system (IMV); middle/inferior to the systemic system.

q.s: A patient with refractory variceal bleeding undergoes a transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt. Two weeks later, he becomes confused with asterixis. Why?
o: Portal blood bypasses the liver, reducing ammonia clearance
e: Correct. TIPS connects portal vein to hepatic vein and can precipitate hepatic encephalopathy.

q.s: TIPS creates a connection between which vessels?
o: Splenic vein and left renal vein
Portal vein and IVC outside the liver
e: Wrong. That is a distal splenorenal shunt.

q.s: The esophageal veins in the portosystemic anastomosis drain into which systemic vein?

A 60-year-old woman with chronic constipation has painless bright red blood dripping into the toilet after bowel movements. Anoscopy shows dilated vascular cushions above the pectinate line. Why are they painless?
o: They receive somatic innervation from the pudendal nerve
e: Correct. Internal hemorrhoids lie above the pectinate line (visceral innervation).

q.s: A 30-year-old man has acute, severe perianal pain and a tender bluish lump at the anal verge. Which nerve carries this pain?
o: Inferior rectal branch of the pudendal nerve
e: Correct. Thrombosed external hemorrhoids below the pectinate line receive somatic innervation.

q.s: A 28-year-old woman with constipation has sharp pain with every bowel movement and bright red blood on the toilet paper. A small tear is seen in the anoderm. Where is it most likely located?
e: Wrong. Atypical (suggests Crohn disease or other causes).
Correct. Anal fissures occur in the poorly perfused posterior midline below the pectinate line.

q.s: Lymph from the anal canal below the pectinate line drains to which nodes?
A tumor arising below the pectinate line is most likely which histologic type?
e: Correct. Ectodermal (squamous) epithelium below the line.

q.s: Arterial supply above the pectinate line comes from which vessel?
o: Superior rectal artery (branch of the IMA)

q.s: Venous drainage below the pectinate line follows which route?
o: Superior rectal → IMV → splenic → portal vein
Inferior rectal → internal pudendal → internal iliac → common iliac → IVC

q.s: The pectinate line marks the junction of which embryologic tissues?
Visceral innervation above the pectinate line comes from which source?
Risk factors for internal hemorrhoids include:
Varices of the "gut, butt and caput" in portal hypertension refer to:
o: Colon varices, pilonidal sinus and gynecomastia
Duodenal varices, anal fissures and spider angiomas
Splenic varices, perianal abscess and jaundice
Esophageal varices, anorectal varices and caput medusae

q.s: Lymphatic drainage above the pectinate line goes to which nodes?
The superior rectal vein drains into which vein?
o: Inferior mesenteric vein → splenic → portal vein

q.s: Anal fissures are associated with which dietary factor?
A 25-year-old woman takes a large overdose of acetaminophen. Liver biopsy 2 days later would show necrosis mainly in which zone?
e: Correct. Highest cytochrome P-450 concentration and least oxygen; most sensitive to metabolic toxins such as acetaminophen.
Wrong. Affected first by viral hepatitis and ingested toxins like cocaine.

q.s: A man with right heart failure has a "nutmeg liver." Which zone is most affected, and why?
o: Portal tracts, because of bile stasis
Zone III, because it is least oxygenated
Zone I, because it receives toxins first
Zone II, because of yellow fever
e: Correct. Congestive hepatopathy and ischemia affect zone III first.

q.s: Viral hepatitis affects which hepatic zone first?
Yellow fever characteristically causes necrosis in which zone?
Which cells in the space of Disse store vitamin A and, when activated, produce the collagen of hepatic fibrosis?
e: Wrong. Not the main fibrogenic cell.

q.s: Kupffer cells are best described as:
o: Specialized macrophages in sinusoids that clear bacteria and senescent RBCs

q.s: What fraction of the liver's blood supply comes from the portal vein?
e: Wrong. That is the hepatic artery.

q.s: The apical surface of hepatocytes faces which structure?
e: Correct. The basolateral surface faces the sinusoids.

q.s: Which zone is the site of alcohol-associated hepatitis and has the highest cytochrome P-450 concentration?
Ingested toxins such as cocaine affect which zone first?
The portal triad consists of which structures?
o: Hepatic vein, portal vein, bile duct
Portal vein, hepatic artery and bile duct (with lymphatics)
Central vein, hepatic artery, bile duct
e: Wrong. Central vein is not part.

q.s: A 50-year-old woman has fever, jaundice, right upper quadrant pain and very high lipase. Imaging shows a stone impacted at the ampulla of Vater with dilation of both the bile and pancreatic ducts. What explains both cholangitis and pancreatitis?
o: Stone in the gallbladder neck only
Stone obstructing the common channel of the bile and pancreatic ducts at the ampulla
Stone in the common hepatic duct
e: Wrong. Does not block the pancreatic duct.

q.s: A 68-year-old man has painless jaundice and weight loss. Examination reveals a palpable, nontender, distended gallbladder. Most likely cause?
o: Gallstone in the common bile duct
Adenocarcinoma of the head of the pancreas
e: Wrong. Stones cause a fibrotic, shrunken gallbladder.

q.s: The common bile duct is formed by the union of which ducts?
o: Cystic duct and common hepatic duct
e: Wrong. Form the common hepatic duct.

q.s: Which sphincter controls flow of bile and pancreatic juice into the duodenum?
The central vein drains into which vessel?
Blood in a hepatic lobule flows in which direction relative to bile?
o: Blood flows toward the central vein; bile flows toward the portal triad
Blood toward the triad; bile toward the central vein
Same direction toward the central vein
e: Wrong. Bile flows the opposite way.

q.s: Which hepatic zone is best oxygenated and most resistant to circulatory compromise?
Carbon tetrachloride and rifampin are most toxic to which zone?
e: Correct. Metabolic toxins activated by P-450.

q.s: Hepatic stellate cells become fibrogenic when activated; in the quiescent state they:

rounds.t: Femoral region, inguinal canal, and hernias

q.s: A 70-year-old woman has a painful, irreducible bulge in her right groin below the inguinal ligament and lateral to the pubic tubercle, with vomiting. Which hernia is most likely?
e: Correct. Below the inguinal ligament through the femoral canal; more common in women and more likely to incarcerate.
Wrong. Above the ligament, through the deep ring.

q.s: A 6-month-old boy has an intermittent bulge in the right groin extending into the scrotum when crying. Which structure failed to close?
e: Wrong. Weakness causes direct hernias in adults.
Correct. A patent processus vaginalis causes indirect inguinal hernias (and hydroceles).

q.s: During inguinal hernia repair, the hernia sac is found medial to the inferior epigastric vessels. What type is it?
A direct inguinal hernia protrudes through which region?
An indirect inguinal hernia is covered by which layers?
o: All three layers of spermatic fascia
e: Correct. It follows the path of testicular descent.

q.s: The femoral sheath contains which structures?
o: Femoral vein, artery and canal (deep inguinal nodes), but not the femoral nerve
e: Wrong. The nerve is outside the sheath.

q.s: From lateral to medial, the structures in the femoral region are arranged as:
To obtain femoral venous access, a needle is placed where relative to the palpable femoral pulse?
o: Deep to the sartorius at mid-thigh
e: Correct. The vein lies medial to the artery ("venous near the penis").

q.s: Which spermatic cord layer derives from the internal oblique muscle?
The internal spermatic fascia derives from which layer?
In women, the inguinal canal contains which structure?

A 72-year-old man with chronic cough has a groin bulge that does not reach the scrotum. At surgery, it passes through the superficial inguinal ring only, medial to the inferior epigastric vessels. Cause?
o: Acquired weakness of the transversalis fascia
Congenital defect of the pleuroperitoneal membrane
e: Correct. Direct hernias occur in older men.

q.s: A newborn has respiratory distress, a scaphoid abdomen and bowel sounds heard in the left chest. Cause?
o: Defect of the pleuroperitoneal membrane (congenital diaphragmatic hernia)
e: Correct. Usually left-sided because the liver protects the right.

q.s: A 60-year-old woman with GERD has a barium study showing the gastroesophageal junction displaced above the diaphragm with an "hourglass stomach." Type?
e: Correct. The most common type; associated with GERD.

q.s: In a paraesophageal hiatal hernia, which structure herniates while the GE junction stays in place?
Adult hiatal hernias result from laxity of which structure?
A 55-year-old woman has a painful lump in the lower abdomen lateral to the rectus muscle along the semilunar line. Ultrasound shows a hernia. Which type?
e: Correct. Through the Spigelian aponeurosis, mostly in the lower abdomen where the posterior rectus sheath is absent.

q.s: Which is the most common type of hernia overall?
e: Wrong. More common in women but less common overall.
Wrong. Not most common in adults.

q.s: An indirect inguinal hernia enters the deep inguinal ring in which relation to the inferior epigastric vessels?
Which hernia is more likely to present with incarceration or strangulation?
